key_insight: Optimizing ferrite content and sintering temperature in lead-free Co1.2Ti0.2Fe1.6O4–BaTiO3 composites strengthens interfacial coupling, with 30CTFO–70BTO sintered at 1200 °C giving the best magnetoelectric response.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies a practical route to lead-free multiferroic composites for low-power sensors, memory, spintronic, and actuator devices.
method: Solid-state synthesis of (x)Co1.2Ti0.2Fe1.6O4–(100-x)BaTiO3 composites with x = 10, 20, 30.
Varied sintering temperature to tune densification, grain growth, and phase coupling.
Measured structure, microstructure, dielectric/ferroelectric, magnetic, and magnetoelectric properties.
evidence_signal: XRD/Rietveld confirmed coexisting tetragonal BaTiO3 and cubic spinel CTFO phases, and the highest ME coefficient reported was ~1.28 mV/cm.Oe for 30CTFO–70BTO sintered at 1200 °C.
watch_item: The ferroelectric response is lossy due to leakage from the conductive ferrite phase, so electrical losses may limit device performance and stability.
paper_title: Optimization of magneto-electric properties in Lead-free (x)Co1.2Ti0.2Fe1.6O4 - (100-x)BaTiO3 based composites
